exact_title: TimelyRAG: Semantic-Temporal Hybrid Retrieval for Time-Critical Question Answering in Overlapping-Evolving Documents
authors: Youngeun Nam, Joeun Kim, Hwanjun Song, Susik Yoon, Jae-Gil Lee, Byung Suk Lee
evaluation_metrics: Retrieval and QA metrics on TimelyQABench (verify exact metric script inside repo)
main_contribution: Semantic-temporal hybrid retrieval tailored for time-critical QA over overlapping, evolving regulatory documents; introduces TimelyQABench.
limitations: Focuses on semantic-temporal retrieval ranking rather than claim-level multi-hop coverage tracking or adaptive budget-constrained stopping.
relevance_to_chronoevidence: Primary temporal retrieval baseline and candidate secondary benchmark for overlapping amendments and partial supersession.
verification_notes: Verified via ACL Anthology (2026.findings-emnlp.398) and arXiv:2609.11572v1. Confirm repo license and data access upon cloning.

exact_title: TEMPO: Realistic Multi-Domain Benchmark for Temporal Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval
authors: Abdelrahman Abdallah, Mohammed Ali, Muhammad Abdul-Mageed, Adam Jatowt
datasets_used: TEMPO (HF: tempo26/Tempo) - 1,730 human-authored Stack Exchange queries across 13 domains; 1,605 queries decomposed into 3,976 retrieval steps
evaluation_metrics: Standard IR metrics (nDCG@k, Recall@k), Temporal Precision@k (LLM-as-judge), Temporal Coverage@k (cross-period span)
main_contribution: Multi-domain temporal reasoning-intensive retrieval benchmark with 10 fine-grained temporal reasoning classes, step-wise retrieval plans mapped to gold documents, and dedicated temporal metrics.
limitations: Temporal Precision@k relies on LLM-as-judge (external API cost/bias); does not evaluate claim-level citation verification or abstention.
relevance_to_chronoevidence: Recommended PRIMARY benchmark: natively includes multi-hop step decompositions, cross-period queries, gold document mappings, and official Temporal Coverage@k / Temporal Precision@k metrics.
verification_notes: Verified via ACL Anthology (2026.emnlp-main.291.pdf) and official GitHub repo. Inspect Hugging Face dataset card for exact license before redistribution.

exact_title: FRESCO: Benchmarking and Optimizing Re-rankers for Evolving Semantic Conflict in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Sohyun An, Hayeon Lee, Shuibenyang Yuan, Chun-cheng Jason Chen, Cho-Jui Hsieh, Vijai Mohan, Alexander Min
publication_status: Preprint (submitted April 17, 2026; NOT confirmed in EMNLP 2026 proceedings)
datasets_used: FRESCO (7,316 queries across 2 query types from Wikipedia revision histories; 1 positive + 50 timestamped hard negatives per query)
evaluation_metrics: Re-ranking metrics over binary relevance labels (1 positive vs. 50 temporally conflicting hard negatives)
main_contribution: Formalizes Evolving Semantic Conflict, demonstrates existing re-rankers favor semantically rich but factually obsolete passages, and proposes Pareto instruction optimization for LLM re-rankers.
limitations: Single-positive re-ranking setting (1 positive per query); does not cover multi-hop evidence aggregation, partial clause amendments, or adaptive stopping.
relevance_to_chronoevidence: Directly motivates ACEC's separation of semantic relevance from temporal validity and informs temporal conflict stress-test design.
verification_notes: Verified on arXiv (2604.14227). Corrected status from playbook draft's informal 'EMNLP 2026' label to Preprint.

venue: Proceedings of ACL 2026 (Volume 1: Long Papers, pp. 25735-25760)

datasets_used: Temporal QA / outdated-knowledge RAG benchmarks (inspect full PDF for exact list)
evaluation_metrics: Retrieval and QA accuracy under temporal hallucination (inspect full PDF)

exact_title: HoH: A Dynamic Benchmark for Evaluating the Impact of Outdated Information on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jie Ouyang, Tingyue Pan, Mingyue Cheng, Ruiran Yan, Yucong Luo, Jiaying Lin, Qi Liu
venue: Proceedings of ACL 2025 (Volume 1: Long Papers, pp. 6036-6063)
datasets_used: HoH-QA (constructed via token-level diffing + LLM semantic screening across Wikipedia snapshots with mock search engine)
evaluation_metrics: RAG answer accuracy and retrieval robustness under outdated-document interference
main_contribution: Large-scale dynamic benchmark with explicit annotations for outdated vs. current evidence demonstrating severe RAG degradation when stale documents coexist with current facts.
limitations: Primarily evaluates single-fact factual updates from Wikipedia rather than multi-hop partial policy amendments or adaptive budget stopping.
relevance_to_chronoevidence: Strong secondary/stress-test benchmark with open repository for testing outdated-evidence resistance.
verification_notes: Verified via ACL Anthology (2025.acl-long.301), arXiv:2503.04800, and GitHub (0russwest0/HoH). Check repo license upon cloning.

exact_title: GroundRAG: Evidence-Verified Multi-Hop Reasoning on Lightweight Graphs
authors: Jinjie Hao, Guixuan Zhang, Ying Huang, Jie Liu, Shuwu Zhang
official_repository: Unverified (inspect ACL PDF directly for repository URL)
evaluation_metrics: LLM-judged accuracy (73.8% HotpotQA, 69.2% 2WikiMultiHopQA, 44.3% MuSiQue) and grounding failure code distributions
main_contribution: Operationalizes Reasoning Chain Hallucination (RCH) via four grounding failure codes and enforces evidence verification over a lightweight passage-sentence-entity tri-graph before generation.
limitations: Evaluated only on static multi-hop QA benchmarks (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue); does not model temporal validity, supersession, or evolving conflicts.
relevance_to_chronoevidence: Closest structural peer on multi-hop evidence graph verification; highlights the exact gap ChronoEvidence fills by combining graph verification with temporal provenance and budget-aware adaptive stopping.

exact_title: The Bottleneck Is Retrieval, Not Reading: Diagnosing Evidence-Based Generation with RAG for Long Context Question Answering
authors: Debopriyo Banerjee et al. (6 authors; verify full author list directly in arXiv PDF)
publication_status: Preprint (submitted October 18, 2026; NOT confirmed in EMNLP 2026 proceedings)
datasets_used: Long-context QA and multi-needle grounding benchmarks (verify exact subset in repo)
evaluation_metrics: Answer accuracy (Ans) vs. joint Answer+Evidence grounding accuracy (Ans+Evid)
main_contribution: Demonstrates empirically that RAG's primary bottleneck is multi-hop evidence coverage rather than single-hop recall, and exposes the grounding gap between answer accuracy and evidence attribution.
limitations: Diagnostic study on long-context EBG; does not propose a temporal evidence-coverage controller or adaptive retrieval stopping policy.
relevance_to_chronoevidence: Provides direct empirical justification for ChronoEvidence's central thesis: tracking multi-hop claim coverage and evaluating joint answer+evidence grounding.
verification_notes: Verified on arXiv (2610.26951) and GitHub (debobanerjee/LC-EBG). Corrected playbook draft's informal 'Evidence-Based Generation (EMNLP 2026)' label to Preprint.

exact_title: MTIMEFACT: Improving Large Language Models for Multi-Hop Temporal Fact-Checking
authors: SCUNLP authors (verify exact author list directly from ACL Anthology PDF)
datasets_used: MTIMEFACT / MTIMEFACTCORPUS (dynamic multi-hop temporal fact-checking structured into a Temporal Knowledge Graph)
evaluation_metrics: Multi-hop temporal fact-checking accuracy and evidence synthesis metrics
main_contribution: Introduces a dynamic multi-hop temporal fact-checking benchmark and Temporal Knowledge Graph corpus showing LLMs struggle when truth values evolve across timelines.
limitations: Live web retrieval component (Tavily) complicates strict fixed-corpus reproducibility unless evaluated on frozen corpus snapshots.
relevance_to_chronoevidence: Strong related work validating multi-hop temporal graph reasoning and a potential diagnostic source of evolving claims.
verification_notes: Discovered and verified via ACL Anthology (2026.emnlp-main.979.pdf) and GitHub (SCUNLP/MTimeFact).

exact_title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity
authors: Soyeong Jeong, Jinheon Baek, Sukmin Cho, Sung Ju Hwang, Jong Park
venue: Proceedings of NAACL 2024 (Volume 1: Long Papers, pp. 7036-7050)
datasets_used: Open-domain single-hop and multi-hop QA datasets (e.g., SQuAD/NQ/TriviaQA, HotpotQA/MuSiQue/2Wiki)
evaluation_metrics: EM, F1, Accuracy, and inference latency/efficiency (Time/Query)
main_contribution: Trains a query complexity classifier to route questions dynamically among no-retrieval, single-step RAG, and multi-step iterative RAG.
limitations: Static upfront routing based on question complexity only; does not inspect intermediate claim coverage, temporal validity, or conflicting evidence during retrieval.
relevance_to_chronoevidence: Core adaptive-retrieval ancestor: contrasts upfront complexity routing with ACEC's closed-loop claim-coverage stopping controller.
verification_notes: Verified via ACL Anthology (2024.naacl-long.389) and GitHub (starsuzi/Adaptive-RAG).

exact_title: DRAGIN: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Real-time Information Needs of Large Language Models
authors: Weihang Su, Yichen Tang, Qingyao Ai, Zhijing Wu, Yiqun Liu
venue: Proceedings of ACL 2024 (Volume 1: Long Papers, pp. 12991-13013)
official_repository: Unverified (inspect ACL PDF directly for repository URL)
datasets_used: 4 knowledge-intensive multi-hop/long-form generation datasets (evaluated with LLaMA-2-Chat etc.)
evaluation_metrics: Answer EM/F1 and generation quality across multi-round retrieval
main_contribution: Triggers dynamic retrieval during generation using Real-time Information Needs Detection (RIND: token uncertainty + attention significance + semantics) and self-attention query formulation (QFS).
limitations: Token-level generation uncertainty can be miscalibrated on outdated facts (high confidence in stale parametric knowledge) and ignores temporal provenance or claim-level citation completeness.
relevance_to_chronoevidence: Key contrast for stopping/triggering policies: ACEC replaces pure token uncertainty with explicit claim-level coverage C(q), temporal consistency T(q), and uncertainty U(q).

exact_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
authors: Akari Asai, Zeqiu Wu, Yizhong Wang, Avirup Sil, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
datasets_used: PubHealth, ARC-Challenge, TriviaQA, PopQA, ASQA, FactScore
main_contribution: Trains an LM with reflection tokens to adaptively decide whether to retrieve, critique passage relevance/support, and verify generation utility.
limitations: Requires fine-tuning a specialized generator/critic LM; lacks explicit multi-hop claim decomposition, document versioning, and temporal validity intervals.
relevance_to_chronoevidence: Foundational self-reflective RAG baseline; ACEC operates as a model-agnostic retrieval controller without fine-tuning a foundation model.
verification_notes: Verified via OpenReview (hSyW5go0v8) and GitHub (AkariAsai/self-rag, MIT License).

exact_title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations
authors: Tianyu Gao, Howard Yen, Jiatong Yu, Danqi Chen
datasets_used: ASQA, QAMPARI, ELI5 (Wikipedia and Sphere corpora)
evaluation_metrics: Correctness (EM/F1/QA), Fluency, Citation Recall, Citation Precision (NLI-based entailment)
main_contribution: Establishes the standard reproducible benchmark and automatic NLI-based evaluation protocol for statement-level citation recall and precision.
limitations: Static corpora without evolving document versions, amendments, or temporal validity conflicts.
relevance_to_chronoevidence: Supplies the formal claim/statement-level citation recall and citation precision evaluation protocol adopted by ChronoEvidence.
verification_notes: Verified via ACL Anthology (2023.emnlp-main.398) and GitHub (princeton-nlp/ALCE).
